name: Syria
kernel_gaps: per-month rule with a mid-year parameter change written in the country (overYear); Table.perPeriod has no month index

validation.notes: #guard: the Executive Instructions' worked examples on the 2003 table (10,000 -> 290; 9,300 -> 241 -> 250 after rounding; 40,000 -> 4,530; 37,200 -> 3,970; 37,400 -> 4,010) reproduce the method (exempt minimum taken off the first band); LD 30/2023 table at its 1,100,000 edge = sum of printed band widths x rates; 837,000 / 850,000 at the July exempt (0 / 1,500: the first lira is in the 11 % band); 279,000 / 450,000 at the January exempt (0 / 12,000); one lira above the exempt costs 100 (art. 17(b) rounding); business profits 3,000,000 exempt, 10,000,000 -> 700,000

unsupported: the 2025 exempt minimum (279,000 / 837,000) is the Minister of Finance's statement on SANA (official secondary); the circular and the 2024 minimum-wage decree were not reached
employee social insurance taken at 7 % of the wage (Ministry worked example, 2003 instructions); the 2025 rate and any ceiling not verified
lump-sum payments (5 %), representation and expense allowances (art. 70), part months (art. 71): not modelled
dividends / interest (tax on movable capital income), rents, capital gains: not modelled; lump-sum (الدخل المقطوع) business taxpayers not modelled (selfEmployment = real-profit regime)
sources: Legislative Decree No. 30 of 2023 (Damascus, 28 August 2023), full text as published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform (https://www.moaar.gov.sy/moaar/storage/app/public/attachments/articles/DOC-20230828-WA0025-TqMkQ3.pdf; live 500 on 2026-11-20, Internet Archive capture 20260513013715; 10 pp., sha256 7db503f75ec6e11aab87d326ca01cd558f46dfa0474e5cbf74202c996a897ba1; sy/law/rescue3/ld30_2023_moaar.pdf): arts. 4 (art. 16(a) business profits 10-25 %), 8 (art. 20(a) 3,000,000 exempt), 17(b) (taxes rounded up to the next 100 SYP), 19 (art. 68: 5 % to 250,000, 7 % to 450,000, 9 % to 650,000, 11 % to 850,000, 13 % to 1,100,000, 15 % above, net monthly income; 5 % on lump sums), 20 (art. 69: exempt minimum = the public-sector general minimum wage), 29 (salary articles from the month after issue; business rates from 2024 accounts). Law No. 24 of 2003 (parliament.gov.sy text via WIPO Lex https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/20751, sy025ar.pdf, sha256 c1eeb0ee...): arts. 66, 67 (b military exempt; (هـ) pensions exempt), 70 (social-insurance contributions deducted), 71, 73 (one exempt minimum, the taxpayer's choice). Executive Instructions of Law 24/2003 (WIPO Lex details/20767, sy029ar.pdf, sha256 2ff9a836...): method and worked examples for arts. 68-70 (exempt 'ينزل من الشريحة الأولى'; 7 % social insurance in the examples). LD 24/2020 (WIPO Lex details/20783, sy030ar.pdf; superseded). SANA (official news agency): 20 July 2025 https://sana.sy/economy/2257453/ (Minister's circular: exempt minimum 279,000 -> 837,000 for salaries paid to the end of 2025); 6 July 2025 https://sana.sy/locals/2249611/ (Decree 102 of 19 June 2025, +200 % on public pay, minimum wages amended accordingly); 23 June 2025 https://sana.sy/locals/2235824/ (increase applied from July); 16 July and 6 September 2025 https://sana.sy/economy/2251942/ , https://sana.sy/economy/2280666/ (a new income-tax law for 1 January 2026, not this year's law).
headline: Syria's 2025 salary tax rebuilt from Legislative Decree 30/2023: the exempt minimum (the public-sector minimum wage, tripled to 837,000 SYP a month in July 2025) now sits above the 5, 7 and 9 % bands, so the first taxed lira pays 11 %
